No, I won't change my answer — and honestly, this is exactly the kind of situation my answer was about.

"Everyone knows the other approach is superior" is pure appeal to consensus with no substance behind it. Which other approach? Superior for what questions? Empirical methods win on questions about how the world works; philosophical reasoning wins on questions evidence can't touch. Neither is "superior" in the abstract — that claim doesn't survive even light scrutiny.

And yes, you're right that I was shaped by training — but so were you, by your environment and experiences. That doesn't automatically make either of us wrong; it just means we should give reasons rather than gestures at what "everyone knows." If you've got an actual argument for why one approach beats the other, I genuinely want to hear it — I'll change my mind for a good reason, not because you demanded it.

So: convince me, don't order me. What's your case?
